selected_rows: The main data source for this analysis is the English Indices of Deprivation 2019:
The English Indices of Deprivation provide information on the prevalence of multiple types of deprivation in England at the Lower Layer Super Output Area (LSOA) level, and the local authority
level. The focus of the accompanying release is income deprivation.
This is information on income deprivation at the lower layer super output area (LSOA) level in England. It is taken from
, File 7: all ranks, deciles and scores for the indices of deprivation, and population denominators.
The key metric is 'Income Score (rate)', which gives the proportion of the population in each LSOA which is income deprived (see

To keep the size of this file manageable, we have removed columns of data relating to non-income deprivation such as health, education, crime, and living environment. All such data
is available in File 7 mentioned above.
This is information on income deprivation at the local authority level in England. It is taken from
local authority district summaries, 'Income'. The key metric here is 'Income - Average score' which is the population weighted average of the 'Income Score (rate)' for each lower
layer super output area within each local authority. This gives the overall level of income deprivation for that local authority.
This sheet gives the data for the rural-urban classification for each English local authority in 2011, available for download from
. There have been boundary changes since 2011,
meaning five current English local authorities are unclassified: Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole; Dorset; East Suffolk; Somerset West and Taunton; and West Suffolk. Since 2011, Shepway
has changed name to Folkestone and Hythe.

The deprivation gap for each local authority is calculated by subtracting the lowest 'Income Score (rate)' from the highest 'Income Score (rate)' within that local authority.
